item.title: Differences between MTF Omega-7 and MTF Alpha-9: Re: Differences between MTF Omega-7 and MTF Alpha-9
item.content:encoded:
Omega-7 was a much earlier version of the team that was disbanded after SCP-076 (who was a member) went berserk and an entire Site was nuked to stop him. I know you said you didn't want to read details, but the story is here. It's a lot shorter than the Alpha-9 stuff.

Alpha-9 comes from the Resurrection canon, where the idea of an anomalous humanoid SCP MTF was, well, resurrected. SCP-105 is the only member of Omega-7 who is also in Alpha-9. I don't know the current state of the Resurrection canon, but I'm pretty sure they aren't actually fully approved and in action in that canon.

A word to the wise: Outside of the fiction, most SCPs that were in Omega-7 or were written to be in Omega-7 were deleted due to low quality. If you're thinking about writing a humanoid SCP into an MTF, be careful, you're heading into rough waters.

Honestly, most of the anomalous humanoids I know of in MTFs have their own specific MTFs instead of being in Alpha-9, and even then you still need to justify it. For example, Tau-5 sees a lot of use beyond their original stories, whereas I'm pretty sure Alpha-9 is only talked about in that particular canon.

item.title: Hearts and minds?: Re: Hearts and minds?
item.content:encoded:
Now, I know the obvious answer is no, they don't care about hearts and minds.

I feel like this is an oversimplification of the Foundation's worldview, honestly — they do have a strong sense of morality, but they're pathologically obsessed with injustices being done for the greater good. The atrocious acts you allude to aren't really done unthinkingly; presumably, someone at the top had to submit a request to the Ethics Committee, who weighed the risk and the reward and the necessity, and then gave the okay.

On an individual level, that's why you see personnel reacting so violently to things like Montauk, since they recognize the obvious inhumanity of it but also accept that their higher-ups have decided that it's for humanity's best. I imagine the same process would play out in your hypothetical retrieval mission, where it depends on someone in the chain of command weighing the risks and giving the order.

item.title: Hearts and minds?: Hearts and minds?
item.content:encoded:
Now, I know the obvious answer is no, they don't care about hearts and minds. The Foundation is an organization based on the utmost secrecy and regular commits atrocious acts against relatively innocent civilians, so outside of the Broken Masquerade canon they don't concern themselves with a public image.

But what I'm asking about is do they care about the hearts and minds of their own people? Many articles suggest they do to some extent. The entire point of SCP-231 is how far the Foundation is willing to go and the psychological toll it takes on their personnel. So to what extent does morality dictate their actions?

Suppose an MTF is on a mission and one of their guys gets grabbed by something. Mission Control can tell from his vitals that he's injured but still alive, maybe he's even calling for help over the radio. I feel like on any ordinary military mission, rescuing an injured teammate would take priority, but if the Foundation sent in a team then chances are they're already prepared to lose them all. So what would they do? Would they shut off the downed agent's radio and instruct the team to continue the mission? Can they expect their agents to be loyal if they know the Foundation won't bother to save them if they get in trouble? If there are any articles that feature a situation like this, please feel free to tell me, I'd love to read them.

And another thing, do SCP objects that are more subjectively "evil" get treated as higher risks? For example, would an entity like SCP-4666 that targets children be a higher priority than other uncontained SCPs simply because humans are more protective of their young?

I apologize if this is a conversation that's been had before, but the internal morality of the Foundation is a subject that fascinates me, and I'd love to hear people's thoughts on it. Thanks!

item.title: Is there a Seth: Is there a Seth?

Both have strong implications that they are Cain and Abel from the Book Of Genesis. Is there an SCP or Tale involving him or has he yet to enter/be discovered in the Foundation World?

item.title: SCP Number Assignment: SCP Number Assignment
item.content:encoded:
What is the canon behind the assignment of numbers to objects?
The foundation has a large number of objects that they contain/monitor with some files being as recent as a year while others dating back decades. There seems to be no particular chronological order to the numbers assigned to a given SCP (ie a 5th series scp could be in the foundations possession since the 70's while one of the original 1st series could only date back to the early 2000's . Now obviously this just a by product of how the out-of-universe site operates, but I was wondering if there was an in-universe explanation for this. Any additional info on the subject is welcome as well :)
